samples.question: This picture contains four small square tiles, arranged as the four corners of one wide two-by-two block with plenty of empty background between them. Every tile has a solid dark border enclosing a four-by-four grid of sixteen equal square cells, and each cell is either dark (the same tone as the border) or pale (the same tone as the tile's background). Exactly one corner of each tile's border is broken by a pale square notch. Carry out this operation. First turn each tile in place, by a quarter turn at a time, until that tile's notched corner is its top-left corner; the tile's sixteen cells turn with it. Leave each tile in its own corner of the two-by-two block: the tile at the top left of the block stays top left, and so on. Then read the four turned tiles together as one eight-by-eight grid, with each turned tile supplying the four-by-four quadrant that matches its place in the block. The dark cells of that eight-by-eight grid form exactly one symbol: 'plus' is a thick upright cross of two central rows crossing two central columns, 'box' is a hollow square ring one cell in from the outer edge, 'hourglass' is a full top bar and a full bottom bar joined by a narrow waist of two crossing diagonals, and 'diamond' is a tilted outline square through the edge midpoints with its centre filled. Every tile shows exactly five dark cells whichever symbol is present, so no tile and no count of dark cells reveals the symbol on its own, and the symbol is not visible anywhere until all four tiles have been turned. Which symbol do the dark cells form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, box, hourglass, diamond.
